newsitem.title: USA: BPA raises Monday peak firm power prices by $2/MWh.
newsitem.headline: BPA raises Monday peak firm power prices by $2/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) continued to offer 200 megawatts of peak firm power for Monday delivery but raised prices by $2.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Friday.
BPA offered Monday peak firm power for Northwest deliveries at $19.00 per MWh and at $21.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
BPA continued to offer an unlimited volume of light-load firm power for Monday, as well as Saturday and Sunday, at $9.00 for both the Northwest and COB.
BPA prices for non-firm power during early morning and late night hours for all three days were also unchanged at $7.00 for Northwest and $8.00 at COB.
Monday non-firm power during hours ending 0600, 0700 and 2300 PDT was unchanged from Friday prices at $10.00.
For Saturday and Sunday, BPA offered peak firm power at $13.00 to $16.50, while peak non-firm was offered at $11.50 to $17.00.
